Decretum episcoporum et aliorum sapientum de Kantia de pace observanda.
The decree of the bishops and other councillors in Kent, concerning measures for the preservation of the public peace.
div.note: Latin only (Quadripartitus); Liebermann prints no German translation. Liebermann's text is from K (Cotton Domitian A VIII?) compared with Co, Or, Jl (Julius C II), T and the group MHkBr. ‘Litera missa regi Adelstano per episcopos et alios dominos Kancie’ is written in red at the foot of the page in T.; F: corrected against Liebermann, Gesetze I (date in the running heads); Wormald, Making of English Law I, October 2026 (was “c.928–c.938; after I & V As (Attenborough)”, now “c.928–c.938 (Liebermann); after I & V As (Attenborough); after V As, before VI As 12 (Wormald)”); F: corrected against Liebermann, Gesetze I (date at the head of the text); Wormald, Making of English Law I; Whitelock, English Historical Documents I, October 2026 (was “c.928–c.938 (Liebermann); after I & V As (Attenborough); after V As, before VI As 12 (Wormald)”, now “c.928–c.938 (Liebermann, I p. 170); after I & V As (Attenborough); after V As, before VI As 12 (Wormald, MEL pp. 439–40)”); BQ: page of each of Liebermann’s texts and of his German, checked against Liebermann, Gesetze I (our double-read transcription), October 2026 (e.g. was “(empty)”, now “Q 170”; 16 rows of III As); V: page of the modern editor’s text / translation, checked against Attenborough (our double-read transcription), October 2026 (e.g. was “(empty)”, now “142 / 143”; 16 rows of III As)

Kancia Lond (stets c statt t vor ia, io, ie); Cantia Co T; Kent übergeschr. M [wohl Cent Original]
Kancia Lond (always c instead of t before ia, io, ie); Cantia Co T; Kent written above M [probably Cent in the original]

Die Überschrift — in Rs steht reliquorum statt aliorum — hatte jedenfalls im Originalbriefe nichts Entsprechendes. Es ist fraglich, ob sie überhaupt aus dem Agsächs. übertragen ist; sapientes (s. Wb) für ‘Provinzialtag-Vorsitzende, Gerichtsobere’, braucht Q zwar öfter, wo er witan übersetzt, doch auch in seinem eigenen Lateinischen Buche Hn; das Wort entscheidet also hier nicht. Wahrscheinlich wurde sowohl die Überschrift in Lond wie die in T erst aus dem Lateintext geschöpft und gehört, da sie der letzten Rez. fehlt, nicht einmal dem Quadr.-Original

The heading — in Rs reliquorum stands instead of aliorum — certainly had no equivalent in the original letter. It is doubtful whether it was translated from the Anglo-Saxon at all; Q does indeed often use sapientes (see Wb) for ‘presidents of the provincial assembly, heads of the court’ where he is translating witan, but also in his own Latin book Hn; so the word is not decisive here. Probably both the heading in Lond and that in T were derived only from the Latin text and, since they are lacking in the last recension, do not belong even to the original of the Quadr.

zu I 170{**} Z. 2. Die Rubrikenliste stand jedenfalls nicht im Originaltexte Q’s. Der Name Æþelr[ed] mag zwar Schreibfehler sein. Aber da sie Lond T spurlos fehlt, ist sie vermutlich, wie die zu manchem anderen Stücke, erst bei Q’s jüngster Rezension hinzugefügt. Sie ist an mehreren Stellen sachlich ungenau, verrät nichts Agsächsisches im Stil, konstruiert vielmehr echt Lateinisch alles bis VI in Einen Satz

on I 170{**} l. 2. The list of rubrics was certainly not in Q’s original text. The name Æþelr[ed] may, it is true, be a scribal error. But since the list is wholly absent from Lond T, it was presumably, like those to many another piece, added only in Q’s latest recension. It is factually inaccurate in several places, betrays nothing Anglo-Saxon in its style, and on the contrary constructs everything up to VI in genuinely Latin fashion as a single sentence
der Gen. hängt von gratias in der Überschrift zur Rubrikenliste ab
the gen. depends on gratias in the heading to the list of rubrics
Nur im Reich erfolgt die Strafversetzung c. 6
The punitive removal in c. 6 takes place only within the realm
Nur 120 Schill. Strafe fordert c. 7. Der Rubrikator kombiniert wohl c. 6 mit missverstandenem abhinc exeat
c. 7 demands a fine of only 120 shill. The rubricator probably combines c. 6 with a misunderstood abhinc exeat

Liebermann dates this document c. 928—c. 938. The ‘bishops’ would then be Wulfhelm of Canterbury (see I As. Pr.; As. Ord. Pr.; II As. Epilogue) and Cyneferth (or his successor Burgric), Bishop of Rochester.
